concepts.title: Positive-definite kernels & the kernel trick
concepts.blurb: A kernel $k(x,y)$ is positive-definite iff every Gram matrix $[k(x_i,x_j)]$ is PSD. Mercer's theorem makes $k(x,y)=\langle\varphi(x),\varphi(y)\rangle$ an inner product in a feature space, so any inner-product algorithm runs nonlinearly by swapping in $k$ — the kernel trick.

concepts.title: Reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces
concepts.blurb: The RKHS $\mathcal{H}_k$ is the Hilbert space where evaluation $f\mapsto f(x)$ is bounded; Riesz then gives a representer $k(x,\cdot)$ with the reproducing property $f(x)=\langle f,k(x,\cdot)\rangle$. Moore–Aronszajn: every PD kernel determines a unique RKHS.

concepts.title: The representer theorem
concepts.blurb: Minimizing $\sum_i L(f(x_i),y_i)+\lambda\lVert f\rVert_{\mathcal{H}}^2$ over an infinite-dimensional RKHS has a solution living in the finite span $\{k(x_i,\cdot)\}$, so $f=\sum_i\alpha_i k(x_i,\cdot)$. Kernel ridge regression solves $\alpha=(K+\lambda I)^{-1}y$.

concepts.title: Support vector machines
concepts.blurb: The max-margin classifier minimizes $\tfrac12\lVert w\rVert^2+C\sum\xi_i$; its Lagrangian dual is a QP in $\alpha$ touching the data only through $k(x_i,x_j)$. Support vectors are the points with nonzero $\alpha_i$, and the margin bound explains its dimension-free generalization.

concepts.title: Gaussian processes
concepts.blurb: A Gaussian process is a distribution over functions whose finite marginals are Gaussian with covariance $k$. GP regression returns a posterior mean $m(x_*)=k_*^\top(K+\sigma^2 I)^{-1}y$ and a predictive variance — kernel ridge plus calibrated uncertainty.

concepts.title: Mercer's theorem & feature maps
concepts.blurb: Mercer diagonalizes the integral operator $T_k f=\int k(\cdot,y)f(y)\,dy$: a continuous PD kernel expands as $k(x,y)=\sum_j\lambda_j\varphi_j(x)\varphi_j(y)$, giving an explicit feature map $\varphi(x)=(\sqrt{\lambda_j}\varphi_j(x))_j$. Random Fourier features approximate the RBF kernel via Bochner's theorem.
